clue.text: In season?

parts.note: to season food is to give it taste, so something 'in season' is read as a passing taste, the current fad

explanation.walkthrough: The usual reading of 'in season' is fruit or game being available; the cryptic reading takes 'season' as adding taste, giving the phrase for whatever is briefly popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived craze is said to be the flavour of the month, just as anything in season is only fashionable for a while.

clue.text: Writer thought, 'Shut up!'

parts.note: to have felt something is to have thought or believed it
to pen an animal is to shut it up in an enclosure

explanation.surface: A writer thinks someone should just be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip marker is an instrument for writing, so it is a writer in the crossword sense of a thing that writes.

clue.text: Guide to China's ancient city

indicators.note: to guide something is to steer it around, so the letters of the following words are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A travel guide to an old city in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the city in China, but 'China's' only supplies anagram fodder; the city was in ancient Syria, now Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a major city of the ancient Greek and Roman world, founded by the Seleucids on the Orontes.

clue.text: Thing is, sweetheart, boss is busy working

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, signalling that these letters are jumbled around

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone explains to their darling that the boss is occupied with work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing is' reads like a conversational opener, but 'Thing' alone is the definition. 'busy' rearranges E, BOSS and IS into OBSESSI.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to be fixated on it, so a thing is a fixation or preoccupation.

clue.text: Exercise care carrying around bombs

indicators.note: around tells us the letters taken from inside are turned back to front
the clue words carry the answer within them, so its letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: An instruction to take care when exercising with explosives nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' picks SECAR from exerciSE CARe, and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To bomb along is informal for going very fast, so bombs means speeds along in the same way as races.

clue.text: Did Nick check spaces in folder?

indicators.note: check spaces the letters of the other word apart by sitting within them

parts.note: a document put in a folder has been filed
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A question whether Nick looked at the gaps in a file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name, but in the definition it is the slang verb for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and to filch is to steal something small, so 'did nick' means stole.

clue.text: Diamond's greatest hit in series?

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
a run of results is a series of them

explanation.surface: A singer called Diamond's biggest hit within a run of records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' suggests the singer Neil Diamond, but it is a baseball diamond, the field.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, played on a diamond, the best possible hit lets the batter round all the bases and score.

clue.text: Cheeky artist's preparation for marriage

parts.note: the bottom is made up of the buttocks, jokingly the cheeks
someone who draws pictures is a drawer

explanation.surface: An impudent painter makes wedding plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' looks like impudent but plays on cheeks, the buttocks; 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride traditionally stored linen and household goods for married life in a drawer kept for that purpose, her trousseau.

clue.text: Able to supply Sainsbury's first, they vowed

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, supply means flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new order
first takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A shop promising to stock Sainsbury's goods before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is read as 'in a supple way', bending ABLE, TO and the S of Sainsbury's into a new order. Sainsbury's is a large British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblates are lay people or religious who have dedicated themselves to a monastic order by a vow or promise.

clue.text: Groom takes look round capital

indicators.note: takes means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: to comb hair is to groom it
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bridegroom glances around a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a bridegroom; it is the verb, to tidy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the commercial capital of Sri Lanka and was long its official seat of government.

clue.text: Dominic tribute not popular — somehow it won't set a precedent

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters fall into place in some other order
not tells us these letters are left out of the fodder

parts.note: something popular is in

explanation.surface: A tribute to Dominic is not well liked, yet sets no precedent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes a word for popular out of the fodder before the scramble; obiter dicta are legal remarks made in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an obiter dictum is a remark by a judge in passing, which is not binding on later cases.

clue.text: The best time to work, setters say

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
setters are breeds of hunting dog, and say marks them as an example

explanation.surface: Crossword setters suggest the ideal hour to get working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' looks like crossword compilers but means dogs such as red setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dogs are the leaders or winners in any group, the people at the head of the pack.

clue.text: Movements of American singer unknown — is about to tour

indicators.note: to tour means to go around, so the reversed letters surround the other pieces
about here means turned around, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: Cher is the American singer and actress
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns, here Z

explanation.surface: Cher is set for a world tour, performing pieces of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses and 'to tour' wraps around; scherzi is the Italian plural, as musicians often use.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement in a symphony or sonata; the Italian plural ends in i.

clue.text: See 1
Rate working for police? Coppers quietly resigning

parts.note: someone in is at work, as in working
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

indicators.note: resigning means quitting, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pence
P, piano, is the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: A question about pay for police work, with officers silently leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police officers but means small coins, PENCE; 'quietly resigning' removes the P.
explanation.definitionFit: The incidence of something is how often it occurs, its frequency or rate.

clue.text: Attic maybe calls for conversion, like this one inside

indicators.note: inside places these letters within the rearranged ones
for conversion says the letters are to be changed into another arrangement

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, written to mean like this
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An attic needs converting into a room, like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' looks like a loft but is the adjective for ancient Athens. 'for conversion' turns CALLS into CLASL, with SIC and A going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic Greek was the dialect of Athens, the literature of ancient Greece being an example of the classical.

clue.text: Hope country girl's a sport — endless tease earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the preceding pieces come before the girl's name

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
Tania is a girl's name; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A country girl is a good sport, though she teases without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' is the author Anthony Hope, not optimism; 'endless' turns RIB into RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Put on again for men in bar (female banned)

indicators.note: in puts the men inside the remaining letters
banned means this letter is kept out

parts.note: a reef is a bar of rock or sand just below the sea
a stag party is for men only, so stag means men

explanation.surface: Clothing for men in a pub, with women not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is a reef; 'female banned' leaves REE around STAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To restage a play is to stage it again, to mount a new production of it.

clue.text: Walked on both sides of road — noted repairs

indicators.note: repairs means fixes up, so these letters are put back in a new order
both sides of takes the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone walked on either side of a road and noted where it was being mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairs' reads as a noun but is a verb; it rearranges RD and NOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that has been trodden has been walked on, the past participle of tread.

clue.text: Used bad language very loudly in centre of Leeds

indicators.note: in puts these letters within the others
centre of takes the middle letters of the word, without its ends

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical term for very loudly

explanation.surface: Someone swore loudly in the middle of Leeds, a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To eff and blind is to swear, a euphemism from the letter F standing for the expletive.

clue.text: Royal family member nearly punching you once round mouth

indicators.note: punching means driving into, so these letters go inside the others
round says the word is turned the other way

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is missing

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house of Scotland and England

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family nearly punches someone in the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouth' at the end looks like the target of the punch, but it is the definition, a river mouth; 'round' reverses and 'nearly' drops a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the wide tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea.

clue.text: Picked up nude after driver's warning: 'Don't do it!'

indicators.note: picked up as by a radio means heard, so the words are to be said aloud

parts.note: a golfer driving shouts fore as a warning, and nude is bare; bare after fore gives fore bare

explanation.surface: Someone nude is caught after a driver shouts a warning not to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but a golfer drives off and shouts FORE; 'Picked up' means heard, so FORE BARE is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain from doing something, so the imperative is a call to hold back.

clue.text: This is disappointing — you used to be sexy nurses

parts.note: was is the past of be, so it is what used to be

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word holds the other

parts.note: hot is slang for sexy
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A remark that someone was once attractive, with nurses involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a plural noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is a complete failure, an event or person that lets everyone down.

clue.text: Can Tranmere Rovers finally get points?

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A question whether the football club Tranmere Rovers can earn points at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Tranmere Rovers is an English football club near Liverpool; 'Can' looks like a verb but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tines are the sharp prongs of a fork or antler, each one a point.

clue.text: Scary! It's flashing like a dirty old man

indicators.note: flashing suggests movement and darting about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A frightening sight: a lecher exposing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing' plays on indecent exposure but signals that SCARY IT are rearranged; 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs of Greek myth were lustful woodland creatures, so satyric behaviour is lecherous.

clue.text: Potter's equipment kept by artist (north countryman)

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the following word

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Harry Potter, the boy wizard, uses a wand

explanation.surface: A potter's tools are held by a northern artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests a ceramicist but is Harry Potter. 'countryman' means a native of a country, here from Rwanda.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rwandan is a citizen of Rwanda in central Africa, a fellow national in that sense.

clue.text: Can't stand around outside Nancy's posh residence

indicators.note: outside means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: ca, circa, means around
to be unable to stand someone is to hate them
Nancy Mitford popularised U to mean upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Nancy can't bear to be outside her grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is also a French city, a red herring for a French word; it is Nancy Mitford, the English writer who popularised U (upper-class) and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a large French country house or castle, a grand place to live.

clue.text: Ian presently sick but he may be rallying

indicators.note: sick means unwell or out of order, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Ian is ill right now, but could be recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rallying' looks like recovering from illness, but means trading shots over the net.
explanation.definitionFit: A long exchange of shots in tennis is a rally, so a competitor in one is rallying.
